data.narrative:
Silicon Quantum Computing, a Series A quantum computing company founded by Michelle Simmons, has raised A$83M to date. The quantum computing sector contains a limited comp universe: 3 public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Standard peer-median valuation proved inapplicable here. The quantum computing sector yielded only 5 same-sector comparables total, with zero companies matching Silicon Quantum's stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero in similar valuation tiers. A meaningful peer-median approach requires a minimum of three datapoints within filtered cohorts; this threshold was not met. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial distortion given the heterogeneity of quantum computing business models, maturity profiles, and capital structures across the comp set.

Without sufficient stage-and-tier-matched peers to anchor a triangulated valuation range, this analysis cannot produce a defensible point estimate or narrow band. The primary uncertainty is methodological: the quantum computing sector remains nascent and dispersed, with few companies at comparable funding stages and revenue/commercialization profiles. Future valuation work would require either (1) expansion into adjacent deep-tech hardware sectors for methodological support, (2) accumulation of additional quantum computing Series A datapoints, or (3) pivot to cash-flow or revenue-multiple methods if operational metrics become available.
